title: Word for students on Mac: templates, citations and Lazur for school work in 2026
metaTitle: Word for Students on Mac: Templates, Citations and Tips for 2026
description: Word for students on Mac in 2026: get templates, set up citations, track edits and export a PDF. Ask Lazur for help while you type.
intro: Word for students on Mac is Microsoft's desktop word processor, and it handles papers, reports, citations and PDF export. Current builds need macOS 14.0 or later, and Microsoft's free student plan includes web Word, not desktop Word. This guide covers setup, templates, citations, Track Changes and the spots where Word for Mac confuses people. Lazur can point at menus and explain them out loud while you work.
tldr: Current Word for Mac is build 16.114.4 and needs macOS 14.0 or later.
The free student plan includes web Word, not desktop Word. Ask your school for a desktop license.
Missing templates usually mean Connected Experiences is off. Check Word > Preferences > Privacy.
Track Changes can freeze large files. Split long papers and save a copy before you accept edits.
Lazur circles menu items, explains settings and dictates text. It does not click for you.

blocks.text: Word for students on Mac: which version you actually get

Start with the version, because it decides what you can do. The Word for Mac listing on the Mac App Store shows build 16.114.4, and it requires macOS 14.0 or later. If your Mac runs an older system, the current build will not install. Check your system with Apple menu > About This Mac.

Then open Word and go to Word > About Word to see your build number. Microsoft's Word for Mac help covers Word 2024 and Word 2021 for Mac. Many steps in this guide work the same in both. If a menu looks different from the guide, compare your version with the help page before you hunt for a missing button.
The free student plan gives you web Word, not desktop Word

This is the point most blog posts get wrong. Microsoft's education page says the free Office 365 A1 plan includes the web versions of Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook and OneNote. Desktop Word is not part of A1. Access depends on an eligible education email.

If the plan lapses, you can view documents but not edit or create them. Some articles claim the free plan includes desktop Word. Microsoft's page does not say that. Ask your school whether it gives you a desktop license before the first big paper is due.

blocks.title: Check access before deadline week
blocks.text: Test editing and PDF export a week early. If your plan lapses, Microsoft says you can view documents but not edit or create them.
Templates missing from the New screen in Word for Mac

Many students open Word and see only Blank Document. One Microsoft Q&A thread from September 2024 describes a user with Word for Mac 2019 Home and Student who saw exactly that. A Microsoft moderator said built-in templates stopped shipping with Office 2016. They now come from the internet.

Turn on Connected Experiences to get them. Go to Word > Preferences > Privacy > Manage Connected Experiences, check the features you want, then quit and reopen Word. Microsoft says the setting covers every Office app, so you change it once.

If the gallery stays empty, search for your template at create.microsoft.com and download it. Save the file in a school folder. Open it, then use File > Save As so your paper lives in its own copy. Never write over the template itself.

blocks.text: Styles, margins and a table of contents that updates itself

A paper goes wrong when every heading is only bold text. Use the Styles gallery on the Home tab. Heading 1 marks main sections and Heading 2 marks subsections. Word reads those styles when it builds a table of contents, so page numbers come out right.

Insert the table of contents after the headings are set. Click where it should go, then choose References > Table of Contents and pick a style. After you edit a heading, right-click the table and choose the update option. Do not retype page numbers by hand.

Margins live under Layout > Margins. Line spacing sits under Home > Line and Paragraph Spacing. Set both in the Normal style so every new paragraph follows the same rules. Your instructor's style guide wins over any default Word gives you.
Worked example: a 12-page lab report in Word for Mac
Here is a setup you can copy. The report has a title page, a table of contents and four numbered sections. Follow these steps in order, and check each one before you move on.

items: Set margins and line spacing under Layout and Home first.
Apply Heading 1 to the four main sections. Apply Heading 2 to subsections.
Put the cursor after the title page text and press Command+Return to start a new page.
Insert the table of contents on page two from References > Table of Contents.
Add footnotes as you write with References > Insert Footnote, not at the end.
Export a PDF with File > Save As, then open it in Preview to check every page.

blocks.text: The setup takes less time than fixing one wrong page number by hand. The biggest saving comes from styles. Once the headings are right, the table of contents follows them without help.
Citations and footnotes in Word for Mac

Word has built-in citation tools. Open the References tab and find Citations & Bibliography. Add a source once, then insert it into your text with a style such as APA or MLA. Word builds the reference list at the end when you ask it to.

Footnotes live in the same tab. Put the cursor after the sentence, then choose References > Insert Footnote. Word numbers the notes for you and moves them when you add text earlier. Endnotes work the same way. Microsoft's help covers footnotes, endnotes and bibliographies.

Watch out for last-minute style changes. Word updates the formatting of every citation. It does not check whether the author or year is right. Read each entry against the original before you submit. A missing year looks fine until a marker finds it.
Track Changes for peer review and group work

Track Changes marks every edit, so the other reader sees what you removed and what you added. Turn it on from Review > Track Changes. Accept or reject edits from the Review tab. Pick Simple Markup or All Markup to control how much shows on screen.

Long files slow down. A copy-editor wrote to Microsoft Q&A in February 2024 about a 60-page article of 230 MB. They said the file hung the machine even in Simple Markup, and typing in All Markup stalled. They could not accept all changes to clear the file.

Work around this by splitting the document. Track changes one chapter or section at a time, then combine the files at the end. Save a dated copy before you accept a batch of changes. Keep the final version as a separate file.

blocks.title: Before you accept changes
blocks.text: Accept changes in small batches and save a copy first. A clean backup costs nothing and saves a late-night rebuild.
Copy formatting, AutoText and comments on Mac

Students who move from Windows often look for the Scrapbook. Word for Mac no longer has it. AutoText does the job now. Save a phrase, your name block or a standard citation intro as AutoText, then insert it from the Building Blocks area when you need it.

Format Painter copies a look from one place to another. Select text with the formatting you want, press Option+Command+C, select the target text and press Option+Command+V. A Microsoft Q&A moderator gave those keys as the Mac shortcut.

Comments need more care. A copy-editor said comment text in their setup could not be formatted, and comments needed an open and close step before they stuck. If your instructor's comments look wrong, ask them to send a PDF with the markup visible.
The Copilot button and Connected Experiences in Word for Mac

Some Microsoft 365 installs on Mac now show a Copilot button. Office Watch reported on June 3, 2026 that the Dynamic Action Button got a Move to upper corner option instead of the promised Move to Ribbon. It sits in the top right of the Home ribbon.

The same article says the author found no way to turn it off completely. A Microsoft Q&A question from November 15, 2024 describes Copilot icons, flashing prompts and a top banner. No Microsoft staff member answered in that thread. The workaround people share is Word > Preferences > Privacy > Manage Connected Experiences, then unchecking the boxes and restarting Office.

blocks.title: Connected Experiences affects templates too
blocks.text: Turning off Connected Experiences can also hide online templates. If you need the template gallery, switch the setting back on for a while.
Export a PDF your instructor can open

Most schools want a PDF. Go to File > Save As and choose PDF from the format list. Microsoft's Word for Mac help covers saving or converting to PDF on a Mac. Open the result before you upload it. Fonts, line breaks and table of contents page numbers can shift.

Add a password only if your instructor asks for one. Microsoft's help covers password protection too. A forgotten password means a file you cannot open, so store it somewhere safe before you send the file.
Dictation and snippets for drafts in Word

Typing is slow when your ideas are fast. Hold fn to dictate clean, formatted text at the cursor in any app, including Word. Dictation works best for first drafts and rough notes. Edit tables, formulas and names with unusual spelling by hand.

Snippets save repeat work. Store your name, student ID and a standard citation intro as a snippet, then say it when you need it. A personal dictionary helps with course codes and field terms. Clipboard slots hold text you need to reuse.
Ask Lazur where things are in Word, one step at a time

Hold ⌥⌘ and ask about anything on screen. Lazur answers out loud. Ask where Track Changes is, and Lazur draws a circle and a label around the Review tab item. Ask how to add a footnote, and Lazur guides you one click at a time, waiting for each click.

Lazur does not click buttons, edit your files or operate Word for you. You make each change. For a paper, that keeps the writing yours and keeps you in control of the file. Lazur also drafts and types text, so ask it for an outline, then rewrite it in your own words.
Check your school's AI policy before you use Lazur on graded work. The [Lazur study guide for students](/for/students) explains how students use it for reading and notes.
Mistakes students make in Word for Mac

items: Typing spaces to move text. Use tabs and paragraph spacing instead.
Skipping styles, then fixing page numbers by hand.
Saving over the only copy after accepting changes.
Following a guide written for a different Word version.
Leaving Track Changes on in the final submission.
Relying on web Word after a student plan has lapsed.

blocks.text: The spacing mistake costs the most time. Spaces break when you edit a line. Tabs and paragraph spacing keep text in place. Set them once, and the layout holds after every change.
Google Docs or Word: what the 2022 survey shows

A June 2022 survey asked 750 students at 52 U.S. colleges which document tool they preferred. 86% chose Google Docs and 14% chose Microsoft Word. SADA, a Google Cloud partner, commissioned the survey, and College Pulse fielded it.

Treat that as a preference result, not a usage result. No study in our research shows how many students use Word for Mac. If your course uses Word, learn it well. If you want the Google side, read the [Google Docs guide for students](/for/students/google-docs).

AI use runs alongside both tools. A 2025 arXiv study of one elite US college reports generative AI adoption above 80 percent within two years of ChatGPT's release. That figure covers AI in general, not Word.
Before you submit: a short Word for Mac checklist

items: Confirm the file opens in your installed Word build, not only in the web version.
Turn off Track Changes or accept the final changes.
Check every footnote and reference against its source.
Update the table of contents and check the page numbers.
Export the PDF with File > Save As and open it in Preview.

blocks.text: Run this list in the last hour before a deadline, not the night before. Some errors only show in the PDF, so check that file last. Keep the working copy as a backup.

faq.question: Is Word for Mac free for students?
faq.answer: Not always. Microsoft's free Office 365 A1 plan for students includes the web versions of Word and other apps. Desktop Word is not part of A1, and access depends on an eligible education email. Your school may provide a desktop license, so ask before you rely on the free plan.

faq.question: What macOS version does Word for Mac need?
faq.answer: The current Word for Mac build, 16.114.4 on the Mac App Store, requires macOS 14.0 or later. Check your version with Apple menu > About This Mac. If your Mac runs an older system, check the App Store listing for current requirements before you download anything.

faq.question: Why does Word for Mac show only Blank Document?
faq.answer: Current builds load templates from the internet. Turn on Word > Preferences > Privacy > Manage Connected Experiences, then quit and reopen Word. If the gallery is still empty, download a template from create.microsoft.com and save it in a school folder.

faq.question: How do I turn off Copilot in Word for Mac?
faq.answer: The sources behind this page do not show a full off switch. Some users report that unchecking the boxes under Word > Preferences > Privacy > Manage Connected Experiences, then restarting Office, reduces the prompts. Microsoft has not confirmed that workaround in the thread we checked.

faq.question: Why is Track Changes so slow in Word for Mac?
faq.answer: Large files with many edits can hang the app. A copy-editor reported in February 2024 that a 60-page, 230 MB article stalled even in Simple Markup. Split the document into sections, track changes in each part, and save a copy before you accept a batch of edits.

faq.question: How do I copy formatting in Word on Mac?
faq.answer: Use Format Painter. Select text with the look you want, press Option+Command+C, select the target text, then press Option+Command+V. Word for Mac does not have the Windows Scrapbook. Save reusable phrases as AutoText from the Building Blocks area instead.

faq.question: Can Lazur write my essay in Word?
faq.answer: No. Lazur drafts and types text when you ask, and it can help you build an outline or find better wording. It does not operate Word for you or click its buttons. Check your school's AI rules before you use any AI tool on graded work.

faq.question: Where do I find Track Changes on Mac?
faq.answer: Open the Review tab in the ribbon, then choose Track Changes. Edits then show as marks for the other reader. Use Simple Markup or All Markup to change how much appears on screen. Ask Lazur where the button is if your ribbon looks different.
